facts.text: ACAS X is the TCAS replacement.
The ACAS X minimum operational performance standards RTCA DO-385 and EUROCAE ED-256 were published in October 2018.
facts.quote: The minimum operational performance standards (RTCA DO-385 and EUROCAE ED-256) were published in October 2018 [69].

facts.text: European validation of ACAS X used the CREME encounter model, built based on twelve million flights.
facts.quote: European validation used the CREME encounter model, built "based on twelve million flight[s]"

facts.text: European validation of the ACAS X threat-resolution module involved simulation of close encounters equivalent to billions of flight hours.
facts.quote: validation of the threat-resolution module "involved simulation of close encounters equivalent to billions of flight hours" [68].

facts.text: Simulation was the primary evidence for ACAS X validation, alongside pilot assessment of individual resolution advisories.
facts.quote: Simulation was the primary evidence, alongside pilot assessment of individual resolution advisories [69].

facts.text: ACAS X encounter models rest on long-standing work, including a MIT Lincoln Laboratory model built from nine months of radar data.
facts.quote: The encounter models rest on long-standing work, such as the MIT Lincoln Laboratory model built from nine months of radar data [71].

facts.text: Acceptance of ACAS X was through RTCA and EUROCAE standards and aviation authorities.
facts.quote: Acceptance was through RTCA and EUROCAE standards and aviation authorities.

facts.text: ACAS X is advisory, with the pilot remaining in the loop, rather than automatic braking.
facts.quote: ACAS X is advisory (the pilot remains in the loop), not automatic braking.

facts.text: March 2022 RTCA SC-147 minutes recorded that European encounter-model results suggested ACAS Xa induced more near mid-air collisions than TCAS, whereas MIT Lincoln Laboratory did not see the same disparity.
facts.quote: European encounter-model results suggested ACAS Xa induced more near mid-air collisions than TCAS, MIT Lincoln Laboratory "didn't see the same disparity"

facts.text: Participants in the March 2022 RTCA SC-147 meeting noted that sensor noise had not been assessed in the ACAS Xa encounter-model comparison.

facts.text: Auto-GCAS is automatic ground collision avoidance for military aircraft.
facts.quote: Auto-GCAS (automatic ground collision avoidance, military aircraft).

facts.text: Auto-GCAS research by NASA, AFRL and Lockheed Martin dates to the early 1980s.
facts.quote: Research by NASA, AFRL and Lockheed Martin dates to the early 1980s

facts.text: Auto-GCAS retrofits on F-16 Block 40/50 began in September 2014.
facts.quote: retrofits on F-16 Block 40/50 began in September 2014 [72, 73].

facts.text: Auto-GCAS had a design requirement to be nuisance free; the test lead prioritized ensuring no harm and no nuisance before providing protection.
facts.quote: The test lead said, "It's only if we can make sure we're not going to do any harm, and not be a nuisance, only then will we worry about providing protection" [74].

facts.text: A 2007 NASA release reported 98 percent effectiveness for Auto-GCAS.
facts.quote: A 2007 NASA release reported 98 percent effectiveness [73].

facts.text: Lockheed Martin says Auto-GCAS integration on the F-35 in 2019 occurred seven years earlier than previously planned, thanks to agile development and reuse of F-16 work.
facts.quote: Lockheed Martin says F-35 integration in 2019 came "seven years earlier than previously planned" thanks to agile development and reuse of the F-16 work

facts.text: Lockheed Martin credited Auto-GCAS with saving eight F-16 pilots' lives by the time of F-35 integration in 2019.
facts.quote: with eight F-16 pilots' lives credited as saved by then [75].

facts.text: The compression of Auto-GCAS validation time came after about three decades of foundational work and still required flight testing.
facts.quote: That is a real compression of validation time, but it came after about three decades of foundational work, and flight testing remained.

facts.text: Auto-GCAS is an automatic flight-control recovery and an intervention analogue, rather than object-triggered braking.
facts.quote: Auto-GCAS is an automatic flight-control recovery, an intervention analogue rather than object-triggered braking.
